title: fix(plugin-auth): degraded rate-limit warning names the cache registration that boots
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuACdPWFJTLDcTrByFCHLzqb)_

Fixes #25329

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changed

With no `cache` service registered, `createLazyCounterStore` (plugin-auth `rate-limit-storage.ts`) falls back to a per-process store and warns once. That warning told a multi-node deployment to use "Redis via @objectstack/service-cache". `CacheServicePlugin.init` throws when `adapter: 'redis'` is set ("Redis cache adapter is not yet implemented"), so an operator who followed the warning got a boot failure.

The warning now names the path that boots today, and promises no bundled adapter, so it cannot go stale when one ships:

> a multi-node deployment needs a shared cache — an ICacheService backed by a store every node reaches, registered as the `cache` service (ctx.registerService('cache', impl)) — or each node enforces the limit independently (ADR-0069 D2)

The ADR-0069 D2 reference and the per-caller `degradedImpact` suffix are unchanged. This is fix option (a) of the card. Option (b), implementing the Redis adapter in `service-cache`, is not taken here.

Every caller of `createLazyCounterStore` prints this text: better-auth's rate limit, the per-number OTP send budget, the SMS quotas, and the runtime's inbound and endpoint limiters.

## Files

- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/rate-limit-storage.ts`: the warning text.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/rate-limit-storage.test.ts`: new pin. The warning names the `cache` registration, does not name `@objectstack/service-cache`, does not say Redis, and keeps `(ADR-0069 D2)`.
- `packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.test.ts`: this pin quoted the old remedy (`/Redis via @objectstack\/service-cache/`). It is flipped to the new one plus a negative on `@objectstack/service-cache`.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/otp-send-guard.ts`: a doc comment that repeated the same Redis-via-service-cache claim.
- `.changeset/25329-rate-limit-cache-warning-remedy.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch.

Out-of-bounds files were not touched: `auth-manager.ts` and `packages/spec`. PR #25328 (docs for the same thread) is merged and edits only `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`, `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx` and `docs/HARDENING.md`, so it does not overlap.

## Verification (head ff4e36d9cc)

- Built the closure `@objectstack/runtime^...` plus `@objectstack/plugin-auth` under the verify lock: VERDICT command-exit 0. `dist/rate-limit-storage.js` carries the new text, and no file in plugin-auth `dist/` carries the old text.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test`: Test Files 189 passed (189), Tests 3580 passed, 10 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck`: exit 0, check:test-typecheck OK.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/security/inbound-rate-limit.test.ts`: 25/25 passed. Runtime reads plugin-auth through its `exports`, so this ran against the rebuilt `dist`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0.
- Ablation, one time, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the src remedy was put back to "(Redis via @objectstack/service-cache)". The anchor went 1 to 0 and the blob changed. `src/rate-limit-storage.test.ts` went red, 1 failed / 19 passed, on the new `toContain` assertion. The file was then restored, blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Acceptance notes

These are not filed here, because they are read-only text drift, not a reproduced defect at a public door:
- `README.md:415` lists `@objectstack/service-cache` as "Cache — in-memory and Redis".
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx:522` and `:543` advertise a Redis adapter in the same package.
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx:130` and `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx:720` already say that the Redis adapter is a skeleton.
